gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-hk: Funky and fat-stroked, Groovy keeps its joins thick right where the strokes meet, while Noto Sans HK stays plain sans, with large lowercase and lifted brush ends. That gap is the pair's real draw.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-imperial-: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads approachable and open, its c ending in two tips that point apart like pincers. And Groovy, with its flat, unmodulated strokes and nearly shut c, makes a tighter, sillier counterpart.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-inscripti: Loose, funky, friendly lettering up top. Groovy earns its keep big and brief, where its slit-like c can be admired, while Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian answers with big open eyes on every e and a.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-jp: Groovy's curves never thin out at the turns, giving every round letter a pencil-drawn, cheerful fullness against Noto Sans JP's very tall x-height. Wide-sweeping curves below are what make it feel modern.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Noto Sans Kaithi fills its lines with lowercase that stands nearly as tall as capitals. Groovy, with its narrow c slit and loose tracking, wants to be big, so give it the larger size and let the plain sans follow quietly.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Friendly is Groovy's whole mood, drawn with compass-pencil consistency. It handles loud, loose headlines, while Noto Sans Kannada does the quieter work of gentle capitals and s curves that open wide at both ends.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Funky, with no hairlines anywhere in Groovy. Its near-closed c sits against Noto Sans Kayah Li, a plain sans whose brush ends lift away early, and that clash of tight and open is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-kharoshth: Noto Sans Kharoshthi reads approachable and dark, curves that never close back on themselves laying a thick stripe of lowercase through every line. Over many lines Groovy stays the playful one, its joins staying full where strokes meet.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer reads clean and modern, with notch-wide openings and small letters standing nearly capital-sized, a sharp foil for Groovy's slit c. Groovy's tight shapes make the Khmer ones look even more generous.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Hairline-free and shadow-free, Groovy is loose, funky lettering with that c barely open. Groovy is best at making noise up top, while Noto Sans Khojki's clear, large eye on every e does the quiet explaining.
